title: Topstitch Style Property Editor (ver. 2025.0)
content: Topstitch Style Property Editor Topstitch Property Editor Topstitch Context Menu * * * ## Topstitch Style Property Editor ### Objective Use these options to edit Topstitch styles and materials. **** ### Location Main Menu ▶ Window ▶ Object Browser ▶ (Select) Topstitch Style ▶ Property editor ### Operation Object Browser ▶ Select a topstitch item in the Topstitch Tab. → The properties are displayed in the Property Editor. Properties | Description ---|--- Information | Name | Enter a name for the Topstitch. | Type | Select either OBJ to create a 3D mesh, or Texture to apply the effect as a material. Offset | Select the Offset distance from the dropdown menu in inches, or enter a value in millimeters in the input box. Stitch Count | Select between 1 and 5 stitches. For multiple stitches, you can apply unique material properties to each one. Enable Use Same Specification to apply identical settings, or Use Same Material to use the same material settings across all stitches. Specification | Shape | Select the type of topstitch from the drop-down icon. Click the plus + icon to[ register the topstitch as an OBJ file **(link here)**.](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358155220249) Click the CONNECT icon to open the CONNECT Store and download buttons. OBJ | Texture Bartack | ![bartack_render.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438335426713) | ![bartack.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438330503577) Buttonhole | ![buttonhole_render.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438335994649) | ![buttonhole.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438336244761) Single | ![topstitch_render.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438331382169) | ![default.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438331645081) Overlock | ![overlock_render.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438337029145) | ![overlock.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438337328281) Pickstitch | ![pickstitch_render.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438337596185) | ![pickstitch.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438332674969) Zigzag | ![zigzag_render.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438338110873) | ![zigzag.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438417186585) Set the Length (SPI), Space, and Thread Thickness of the Topstitch. ※Note: SPI stands for Stitch Per Inch, meaning the number of stitches within an inch. For example, 'SPI-4' means there are four individual stitches within an inch. For standard garments, SPI-11 is often used. Material Button / Thread | Type | Set the appropriate fabric type for the topstitch. ---|---|--- Base Color | Color | Select the color of the base color. Base Color Map | Base Color Map | Click the explore button and apply a texture image from the Library/Folder. Desaturate | Desaturate the entire Base Color Map to remove color and convert it into grayscale or black and white. Switch | Color Switch: Easily and quickly switch the color of the texture to a new one without losing the accuracy of the chosen color. ![Switch Color.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438338582553) ※Note: For consistent results, the Base Color Map should contain 1 color. If the Base Color Map contains multiple colors, users may experience unexpected results. Normal Map | Click the explore button and apply a texture image from the Library/Folder. Generate with the PBR texture generator icon. Intensity | Adjust the intensity of the Normal map from -100 to 100. Displacement Map | Click the explore button and apply a texture image from Library/Folder, generated with the PBR texture generator icon. Amount | Adjust the maximum height of the displacement map. The white area of the displacement map shows the maximum height. Shift | Adjust the distance between the displacement map and the garment surface Clipping | Adjust to delete all geometries below the Clipping value. Particle Distance | Adjust the Particle Distance of newly created meshes. Keep Continuity | Extend the adjacent face to eliminate the boundary line. ※ Note: Only applicable to Welded OBJs. Opacity | Adjust the opacity level from 0 to 100. Opacity Map | RGB Mode | The encoded map with alpha value in the RGB channel. Alpha Mode | The encoded map with the alpha value in the alpha channel. Reflection | Roughness | Intensity | Edit fabric gloss by adjusting the Intensity of the Roughness Map | Edit fabric gloss by adding and modifying the Roughness Map. Map | Select the Browse button next to the Map option to add a Roughness Map to the selected Fabric style. Map Intensity | Adjust the Map's Intensity. Invert | Select to invert the gloss of the fabric. When this option is selected, the shiny part becomes dull and vice versa. Reflection Intensity | The greater/lesser the Reflection Intensity value is, the more reflective/dull the material or fabric is, and vice versa. Metalness | Adjust the metallic level. A higher value makes the surface more metallic. Metalness Map | Partially express metallics using a grayscale image. The white parts of the map appear metallic. Configuration | Face | Select the Face of Topstitch. Number of Lines | Set how many lines of Topstitches there are for a single style. Distance | It is possible to adjust the distance between the lines. The unit of length can be set in inches, millimeters (mm), or centimeters (cm). 3D | The Topstitch is more realistic in the 3D window. ![89308cd0-c743-465a-a7e8-153683d5631c](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438417580057) ## Topstitch Property Editor ### Objective Use these options to edit topstitch styles: * Extend: When the start or end point of a Topstitch does not reach or stick out of the Pattern outline, extend it to fit to the outline of the Pattern. * Corner: Set the Topstitch corner type to extend the stitch more smoothly at corners. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Edit Topstitch 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Topstitch ### Operation Find the menu from the location above, and select a topstitch line in the 2D pattern window. → Topstitch properties appear on the Property Editor. Property | Description ---|--- Name | Rename Topstitch. Topstitch Property | Select the Topstitch to edit its properties. Extend | Turn On/Off the settings in Start / End. Corner | Curved | When turned On, the selected Topstitch is now curved and smoothly extended. ![rightangledcorner.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438417837593) ※ Note: Corner settings only apply when connecting with Free Topstitch Sewing. Right Angled | When turned On, the selected Topstitch is now a right angle. Z Offset (mm) | Enter a value in millimeters to set the offset from the pattern surface. ![89308cd0-c743-465a-a7e8-153683d5631c](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438417580057) ## Topstitch Context Menu ### Objective Use these options to manage topstitch, including deleting and renaming. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Window ▶ Object Browser ▶ Topstitch ### Operation Right-click a button in the location panel to rearrange the topstitch list. **Menu** | **Description** ---|--- Delete | Deletes the selected Topstitch style. ※Note: You can also delete them with the Delete Topstitch on the keyboard. A Topstitch Style can only be deleted if there is no Topstitch assigned to it. Delete All Unused Topstitches | Removes unused Topstitches from the Topstitch list. Rename | Rename the Topstitch style. Reset | Resets the properties of the Topstitch style to the Default Topstitch properties.
content_description: The Topstitch Style Property Editor web page provides comprehensive tools for editing and managing topstitch styles and materials in a user-friendly interface.

title: Puckering (ver 2024.0)
content: Create puckering Apply Puckering Edit Puckering Puckering Style Properties Assign Puckering Style Puckering Style Properties Show/Hide Puckering ![89308cd0-c743-465a-a7e8-153683d5631c](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438164865433) ## Create puckering You can create puckering on pattern outlines, inner line segments, and sewing lines. ### ## Apply Puckering ### Objective Apply puckering textures, including normal and base color maps for detailed surface definition and fold points at seams to create realistic-looking fabric gathers and wrinkles along seamlines. ### Operation **Segment Puckering** Select a line segment to create puckering. 1\. Select the Segment Puckering tool via the path below. Location Main Menu → Materials → Puckering → Segment Puckering 2D Window Toolbar → Segment Puckering 2\. Click the segment you want to create a puckering for. **Free puckering** You can create puckering on pattern outlines and internal lines regardless of segment points. 1\. Select the Free Puckering tool via the path below. Location Main Menu → Materials → Puckering → Free Puckering 2D Window Toolbar → Free Puckering 2\. Set the first and last points on the line where you want to create the puckering by clicking the mouse. **Seamline Puckering** You can create a puckering on a pattern seamline. 1\. Select the Seamline Puckering tool via the path below. Location Main Menu → Materials → Puckering → Seamline Puckering 2D Window Toolbar → Seamline Puckering 2\. Click on the Sewing Line to create the puckering. ### End Result → Puckering is created on that line. → You can see the puckering created on the 3D Garment. → For Seamline Puckering, the puckering will appear on one or both Sewing Lines depending on the 'Placement' set in the Puckering Properties. ※Note: In the 2D window, you can create puckering in one step by clicking and dragging an area to include all the desired line segments. Puckering cannot be created twice. ![89308cd0-c743-465a-a7e8-153683d5631c](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438164865433) ## Edit Puckering You can select and modify the puckering applied (move the position, modify the length/width). ### Operation 1\. Select the Edit Puckering tool via the path below. Location Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Puckering ▶ Edit Puckering 2D Window Toolbar ▶ Edit Puckering Object Browser ▶ Select the Puckering Icon in the Object Browser (Ver. 2025.0) ![Screenshot 2025-04-15 132418.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438147484697) 2\. Click & drag to select the line segment or Left-Click on the puckering line to edit the puckering. 3\. To delete the puckering, select the puckering line and press the Delete key on the keyboard. ### End Result → Move Position: Select & drag the puckering line to move the entire line. → Modify Length: Click and drag the end point of the puckering to modify the length. If you right-click while editing the length, a Moving Distance dialogue will appear, allowing you to move it to the desired numerical value. ![89308cd0-c743-465a-a7e8-153683d5631c](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438164865433) ## Puckering Style Properties Set the properties of a Puckering Style. ### Operation 1\. Select a puckering object / line with the Edit Puckering tool. The Properties are displayed in the Property Editor beneath the Object Browser. Edit the selected puckering. **Puckering object properties** **Property** | **Description** ---|--- Name | Changes the name of the puckering object. Puckering Property (ver. 2025.0) | Changes the puckering style. Extend | Extends the start/end of the puckering to the outline of the 2D pattern. Offset | Offset | Adjusts the distance the puckering is spaced from the pattern outline. Include or exclude the width of the puckering from the spacing as needed. Z Offset | Adjust the Z-axis distance of the puckering. Placement | Both Sides | *For Puckering on Internal Lines only. Check the box to have Puckering appear on both sides of the Internal Line. Flip | *For Puckering on Internal Lines only. Check the box to flip the puckering to the other side of the internal line. 2\. Another option is to right-click on the applied puckering with Edit Puckering active to apply the options as needed. **Menu** | **Description** ---|--- Select All With the Same Property | Selects puckering with the same styles as the selected puckering. Assign to New Puckering | Adds and applies a new puckering style. Delete | Deletes the puckering. ※Note: You can also delete by pressing the Delete key on your keyboard. ![89308cd0-c743-465a-a7e8-153683d5631c](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438164865433) ## Assign Puckering Style Applies the Puckering style to the selected Puckering lines. ### **Apply with a generated Puckering style** 1\. When generating Puckering: After selecting a Puckering style in the Puckering window, it will be applied as the selected style when generated. 2\. Apply after Puckering is created: Select a Puckering line and click the 'Apply' button to the right of the Puckering style. **Apply as a new Puckering Style** 1\. Select a Puckering line and add it with the 'Assign' button at the top of the Puckering window. 2\. Select a Puckering line and add it to the 'Assign to New Puckering' menu from the right-click menu. ![89308cd0-c743-465a-a7e8-153683d5631c](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438164865433) ## Puckering Style Properties You can adjust the properties of the Puckering style to achieve different forms of puckering. When you select a Puckering Style in the Puckering window, the Puckering Style properties appear in the Properties window. Open/Save Puckering Styles: You can save and recall styles via the Open and Save buttons at the top of the properties window. **Puckering Style Properties** **Information** | Name | Change the name of the puckering style. ---|---|--- **Material** | There are five presets available: Cotton, Denim, Leather, Nylon, and Polyester. Basic Parameters | Texture | Apply a texture. Desaturation | Use to leave the pattern or texture of the texture image and vary the overall color of the rest of the image. Shadow Intensity | Adjusts the shadow intensity of the texture. Shadow Brightness | Adjusts the brightness of the shadows, leaving the pattern or texture of the texture image. Normal Map | Brings up a normal map to change the appearance of the puckering. Intensity (%) | Adjusts the intensity. Color | Adjusts the color of the texture. Opacity | Adjusts the transparency of the texture. **Specification** | Density % | Adjusts the density of the texture. Width | Adjusts the width. ![89308cd0-c743-465a-a7e8-153683d5631c](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438164865433) ## Show/Hide Puckering You can show or hide the overall puckering. ### Steps 1\. In the 2D window Location Main Menu → Display → Materials → Show Puckering View icon in 2D window → 2D Sewing → Show Puckering 2\. In the 3D window Location Main Menu → Display → Materials → Show Puckering View icon in 3D window → 3D Trims Display → Show Puckering ### End Result → You can show or hide all the created puckering in the window.
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for creating, applying, editing, and managing puckering styles in fabric design, enhancing the realism of garment simulations.

title: Auto Convert to Motion (Ver. 2025.0)
content: ### ### Objective Convert FBX files from external platforms into motion files for Marvelous Designer Avatars. Converted motions are compatible with all Marvelous Designer Avatars. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Auto Convert to Motion ### Operation 1. Select the tool/menu indicated. → Auto Convert to Motion window appears. → Mode is Switched to Animation Mode immediately to check the converted motion. ※Note: An error occurs when Avatars already exist in the 3D window. 2. Select the Gender of the avatar to be converted, open the Motion File (FBX) and click Convert button. You can open FBX files downloaded from platforms such as Mixamo, or your own custom animation file. → Convert it to motion for Marvelous Designer Avatars. 3. Click Play in the Animation Editor to check the converted motion. 4. Click the Save button to save as motion file (MTN). ※ Note: To Move the Avatar and Garment to the location of the first frame of converted motion, load the saved motion file.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for converting FBX files into compatible motion files for Marvelous Designer Avatars, ensuring seamless animation integration.

title: Avatar Editor (ver. 2025.0)
content: Avatar Settings Avatar Size Measure Arrangement Fitting Suit IK Joint ### ![89308cd0-c743-465a-a7e8-153683d5631c](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438255194649) # Avatar Settings ### Objective Adjust the Avatar settings, such as size, measurement, arrangement, fitting suit, and IK settings. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Avatar Editor ### Operation 1. Place an Avatar in the 3D window. The Avatar Editor is accessible only when the avatar is in the 3D window. 2. Select the tool/menu indicated above under Location. → Avatar Editor window will appear. 3. Adjust the properties for the properties below. There are separate tabs for Avatar Size, Measure, Arrangement, Fitting Suit, and IK Joint. ### # Avatar Size Avatar size allows you to create a custom-size avatar with your own measurements. The Marvelous Designer Avatar Editor is powered by real body scan data to help you create realistic body shapes, whether you have a complete size specification or not. ### #### **Size:** Option | Description ---|--- Size | Custom / Presets | Select an Avatar size from the presets, or create an avatar with your desired size by inputting detailed measurements. From the dropdown, presets include standard sizing such as Curvy, Straight, Petite Curvy, Petite Straight, Plus Curvy and Plus Straight for women, and size 34 to 52 Standard for men. Additional size measurements can be added and entered in the "Set Details" from the gear icon. Avatar Name (.avs) | Select the Avatar file. Units of measurement | Select from Millimeter, Centimeter, Inch, Feet & Inch. Set Details (gear icon) | By clicking this icon, you can select and activate currently hidden size measurements. When checked on, they will become available in the Size section for editing. Show all Measurements (list icon) | By clicking this icon, you can view active and hidden size measurements that are not displayed in the editor window. If the measure is not checked on in the Set Details it will be visible, but not editable. Width / Height | The Width/Height categories allow you to select what you want the key measures to be for your size, and Marvelous Designer will then automatically generate a proportionate body shape based on these key measures. For example, if Under Bust and Total Height are selected here, circumference, height, and length measures below will be automatically created or slightly adjusted to maintain a proportional body shape. Link (default) | Size editing for Marvelous Designer avatars is algorithm-based, and by default, measures are linked to help you create a proportional body shape based on real human body scan data. Unlink | You can unlink the proportional editing by clicking the icon to deactivate it. When unlinked, any changes to the key Width/Height measurements will not affect the lower measurements. #### **Shape:** Option | Female | Male | Kid | Baby ---|---|---|---|--- Shape | Hand & Head | Hand | O | O | X | X Head | O | O | O | X Crotch | Width | O | O | X | X Volume | O | O | X | X Hip | Dips | O | O | X | X Volume | O | O | X | X Breast | Shape | O | X | X | X Space | O | X | X | X Height | O | X | X | X ### **Custom Avatar Size (recommended workflow)** 1. Go to Avatar > Avatar Editor to open the editor. Load the Avatar *.AVT and ensure it is the version you want to apply your size to. 2. If you are editing from an existing *.AVS file, click the open icon to select your file. When open, the avatar measures will be displayed in the 3D window. Measures that can be moved will appear as black dotted lines, and non-editable measures will be grey dotted lines. 3. Before entering size data in the editor window, ensure the desired values are available. If not, click the Set Details button to add them and Exit to go back to the main editor. For optimal results, it is recommended to activate only the measurements that you have. 4. Once you have your avatar and desired measures, select your key measures for Width / Height and enter your values. It is recommended to keep the default Link option on, but if desired, click the icon to unlink. 5. Now enter your desired measurements in circumference, height, and length. Note that when linked, Marvelous Designer will make slight automatic adjustments to maintain a proportional body shape. ※Note: When developing categories such as gloves, intimates, and headwear, you have additional options to adjust the head, hands, crotch, and bust to suit your needs. 6. Press Save to save your custom Avatar. After creating a custom size, you have the option to save the size only (*.AVS) or as an Avatar (*.AVT). The steps to modify the measurements of an Avatar are the same whether saving an *.AVT or an *.AVS file. The only difference is the way you open the file. #### **File Format** File name | Description ---|--- Avatar (.AVT) | The *.AVT is a Marvelous Designer native format, which contains all the information related to Avatars, including the model, skeleton rig, sizing, pose, motion, accessories, bounding volumes, and arrangement points. Avatar Size (.AVS) | The *.AVS format contains avatar size information. The Avatar file must be loaded before opening an *.AVS size file. The *.AVS format does not contain any avatar, only size information. ※Note: It is not possible to mix *.AVS files between avatars of different versions, age, or gender. The *.AVS file is only compatible with the avatar on which it was originally created. For example, if you created an *.AVS file using a female V2 Avatar, this will only apply to the female V2 Avatar. Saving in .AVS You can connect the folder you saved to your library and click-drag your different sizes on the avatar of your project file. You can open an .AVS file, using the Folder Icon next to Save in the Avatar Editor. Saving in .AVT If you want to add a custom Avatar in the workspace, open from File ▶ Open ▶ Avatar. ![89308cd0-c743-465a-a7e8-153683d5631c](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438255194649) # Measure You can use 6 types of avatar tape that allow you to create free measures, circumference, linear, and height measurements. Please see the [**Measure manual**](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358154578585-Avatar-Measure-above-ver-10) for additional Measure information. All added measurements can be viewed and renamed in the Measure tab. ※Note: The difference between ‘Basic’ and ‘Surface’ is whether the measure will follow the curvature of the avatar's body or follow a direct line around the widest points. The Basic Tapes are most akin to methods of measuring the body with soft measuring tape, whereas ‘Surface’ will measure along the curved surface of the body. #### **Measure:** Option | Description ---|--- Measure | Name | The default name appears after creating a new measure. Double-click on the text to rename. Delete | Delete the selected Measure. ※Note: You can also use the Edit Measurement tool to select the Tape Measure in the 3D Window and hit either the Backspace or Delete key. Fit to Avatar | Re-fit the measurements when changing its Pose or loading another Avatar's joints. Open | Open a *.MEA file created with other Marvelous Designer Avatars. Save | Save the measurements in *.MEA format to open with other Marvelous Designer Avatars. ※Note:.MEA files should be applied to the same model in the same version. Measurement Type | Toggle the Measurement Type between Basic and Surface to update the type without needing to recreate the measurement. Measurement Information | Measurement Information given is either Tape or Circumference. Basic Length | Check the value when measured with the Basic Measurement tool. Surface Length | Check the value when measured with the Surface Measurement tool. Show | Toggle on or off to show or hide the selected measurement in the 3D Window. Show Length | Toggle on or off to show or hide the selected measurement in the 3D Window. ![89308cd0-c743-465a-a7e8-153683d5631c](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438255194649) # Arrangement Edit, add or delete any of the Bounding Volumes or Arrangement Points in the Arrangement tab. Please see the [Arrangement manual](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/sections/47114831810969) for additional information on how to use Bounding Volumes and Arrangement Points. You can rename any Bounding Volume and Arrangement Point with "NAME_1_L", "NAME_1_R" to maintain symmetry. All arrangement points apart from the Avatar's body are symmetrically set by default. #### **Bounding Volume:** Option | Description ---|--- Board | Name | You can double-click to rename the default name. Add | A new Bounding Volume called “PAN” will be added at the bottom of the list. Delete | Deleted the selected Bounding Volume Reset Bounding Volumes | Reset to the original position Open | Open a pre-saved *.PAN file Save | Save the created *.PAN file to use with other avatars. Joint Name 0 | Set the beginning location of the Joint (X-ray) Joint Name 1 | Set the end location of the Joint (Show Avatar Joint) Height | Set the height Radius X (mm) | Set the horizontal radius Radius Y (mm) | Set the vertical radius Hands/Feet | Toggle on to extend BV's length to Avatar's hands or feet, respectively #### **Point:** Option | Description ---|--- Placement | Name | You can double-click to rename the default name. Add | A new arrangement point named “Arrangement Point” will be created at the bottom of the list. Note that the point is unassigned by default, and you will need to select the BV and X Y positions in the steps below. Delete | Delete the selected Arrangement Point. Open | Open an *.ARR file; this can be used to apply Arrangement points to an *.OBJ avatar. Save | Save as an *.ARR file and open on another Avatar. Note: Some readjustment may be needed when applying to another avatar. Arrangement BV | Selects the Bounding Volume where the Arrangement Point is to be placed. X | Moves the Arrangement Point left and right. Y | Moves the Arrangement Point up and down. Offset | Sets the distance between the Avatar and the Arrangement Point. Wrap Direction | Wrapping can be set to up or down and will determine the direction of the pattern wrap when placed on the Arrangement Point. ![89308cd0-c743-465a-a7e8-153683d5631c](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438255194649) # Fitting Suit 1. Draw lines on the avatar according to the indicated position below. 2. Create the circumference line on the avatar's position following the image. • The pattern of the fitting suit is displayed. • The circumference line on both sides is automatically created symmetrically. 3. After creating all the circumference lines, click the Drape Fitting Suit button. • The fitting suit is draped. Adjust the fitting in the 3D window if needed. Option | Description ---|--- Fitting Suit | Auto Create Fitting Suit | Click this icon to create a fitting suit automatically. If the avatar is not created properly, we recommend creating it manually. Create Symmetric Tape | Toggle on and off to create the draw line symmetric or not symmetric. Delete | Delete the drawing line. Reset | All drawing lines will be deleted. Save | Save as an *.AVT file. **![89308cd0-c743-465a-a7e8-153683d5631c](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438255194649) ** # IK Joint Use IK joint mapping with various avatars to achieve natural movement while ensuring seamless compatibility for motions and poses across all avatars. The avatar must have properly defined joint points. Rigging must include key joints such as shoulders, elbows, wrists, pelvis, knees, and ankles. Joints are categorized into required and optional, and you must map all required joints to ensure proper IK setup. ※ Note: The FBX file must not contain joints with duplicate names, and IK mapping may not apply correctly for creatures or quadruped avatars with non-human structures. Operation | Description ---|--- Open / Save | You can manage the IK data mapped to the avatar as a file. Click Open / Save icon at the top right to open or save IK data as a .iks file. ※Note: IK files are only compatible between avatars that have been mapped. Auto Mapping | If the avatar meets the following conditions, click Auto Mapping at the top right to apply automatic mapping. • If each joint name of the avatar matches that of the Marvelous Designer avatar. • If the avatar is from one of the following platforms: Daz 3D, Adobe Mixamo, Reallusion Character Creator, or Unreal Engine MetaHuman. Set T-Pose | Set the avatar in a T-pose to ensure proper compatibility with Marvelous Designer avatar pose and motion files apply correctly. Adjust the avatar’s joints directly to a T-pose using the gizmo in the 3D window. If the avatar is already in a T-pose, this step can be skipped. Click Set T-Pose button. Reset Pose | If T-Pose is set correctly, this button activates, allowing you to check the Set T-pose when clicked. After adjusting the pose during IK mapping, click this button to revert the avatar to the set T-pose. ****
content_description: This web page provides comprehensive guidance on adjusting Avatar settings in Marvelous Designer, including size, measurements, arrangement, fitting suits, and IK joint configurations for optimal customization and realistic simulations.

title: Enterprise License Management Guide
content: Enterprise accounts are divided into Company ID and End User ID. For Enterprise Accounts, End User IDs (used to access software) are managed by Company IDs. To get better understanding on characteristic of each account and structure, please refer to the link below. * [Account Manual](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358380019737) **How Can I Manage My Licenses?** To manage your licenses, you will first need to login with your Company ID, at a page below. * [Account Login Page](https://www.marvelousdesigner.com/member/signin) On “License Account Admin” you can view all licenses you’ve had in the past, upcoming expiration dates, delete/add end users, purchases licenses, view active end users, etc. You can access License Account Admin upon after the login, by clicking on your profile icon. ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438023097369)![image \(5\).png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47437990997657) _(sample image)_ On your “Dashboard”, you can view weekly average access to licenses, how many times licenses were used, how long do users spend on the software on average and etc. _*Denied access_ Denied Access refers to concurrent access being exceeded by users. For example, if you have 10 licenses, your concurrent access will be for 10 seats. If you are sharing the 10 licenses among 20 people, this feature lets you know that one of the 10 individuals will have to log out if another user needs access, or it may be time for you to purchase additional seats. The data is only valid for the network (floating type) license holders. The contact information is also provided on the left bottom of the screen for regional managers. Regional managers can help you with how to use the License Management services, and answer any questions. Based on the location you have set for your account, you will have different regional managers. If the listed regional managers are out of office, please feel free to contact md.bizdev@marvelousdesigner.com to reach out to the entire business development team. **How Do I Know What Licenses I Have and What Can I Do With Them?** Click on the “License” tab on your left menu which will bring you to this page. ![image \(6\).png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47437977588249) _(sample image)_ **Filter section** In this section, you can search End User IDs or an email address to quickly look for the End User ID you are looking for, set to view active and expired licenses, perpetual/monthly/yearly/trial licenses and different versions of licenses. ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47437977795481) _(sample image)_ **License detail section** In this section, you can see every End User ID under your Company ID. You can view information such as the email address attached to the End User ID, plan type, license type, license count, current software version, and expiration dates. You can also directly add/extend your existing seats, or purchase a new license through this menu option. ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438040393497) _(sample image)_ **Add/extend option** You can add another license to the same End User ID or extend the license period before the period ends. Both actions can only be done before the license expires. **New license option** New License option allows you to renew licenses past the expiration date. This action can only be done after the license expires. **Trade-In option** Perpetual license is eligible for our 'Trade-In' service, which is to convert perpetual license to annual type. Please refer the link below for more detailed information on this. * [Trade-In Policy](https://www.marvelousdesigner.com/support/news?postId=233762c17aa04616bb0367f0f9561371) **License ID (End User) detail section** Clicking the individual license ID (End User) from the previous image on the left hand side, will lead you to the single End User detail page. In this page, you can manage End User IDs by viewing the user details, your password for the End User, the email address and the IP address when the license is being used at corporate premises. ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438008453657) _(sample image)_ **What Else Can I Expect from License Account Admin page?** **User Pool** Within User Pool feature we provide, licenses are now much flexible in terms of management. Please read a separate manual followed by the link below, for better understanding of the usability around this feature. * [**User Pool Manual**](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358149827609) **Invoice** In the invoice section, you can view your past orders and invoices. You can also add and edit your billing address within this section.
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for managing enterprise accounts, detailing the relationship between Company IDs and End User IDs, license management features, and resources for further assistance.

title: User Pool Manual
content: ## **Description:** Userpool is the feature included in the License Account Admin page along with the launch of Marvelous Designer 2024.2 for those that are integrated with CLO-SET. Please read the page in the link below for more information on account integration. [(LINK to the page](https://landing.clo-set.com/allatonce)) Userpool enhances the experience of license management with multiple & single users and provides higher security around the license usage as well. The Userpool can be found and accessed at the left side of the menu bar inside of the [license account admin page](https://www.marvelousdesigner.com/teamconsole). ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438167645209) ***IMPORTANT** In order to access the User Pool, you will need to have your Company ID integrated with CLO-SET as part of our optional One-Step login process. You will need to integrate your Company ID, and End User IDs (License IDs) under your company as well, with a valid working email address in order to operate the Userpool feature fully. Any users who are invited to accounts must be integrated with CLO-SET as well. ## **Offerings:** ### **[Userpool Settings]** **![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438139894937)** **![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438202253977)** * Userpool is set to be enabled as its default upon completing account integration. * From ‘Userpool Settings’, you can also choose to turn it off for a specific License ID if you wish not to share it. * Push the slide bar in order to disable userpool from certain License ID. * If the userpool gets turned off while the selected License ID is assigned with 1 or multiple members, they will be removed afterward. ### **[Add Members]** **:** How to add the members to Userpool? * By License Account admin (Website) **![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438202459161)** **![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438168278297)** * After clicking ‘Add Member’ button, the pop up window will appear * Choose certain License ID that you want to have assigned with members who are in needs of license usage * Type in a member's ID (email address) to assign. This also can be done with multiple number of member IDs at once. * Once the add member procedure is completed followed by the steps above, the member information will appear on the page, and the email will be sent for the verification on the member’s end. * By Software (Marvelous Designer) _*'Auto Add' option has to be on for this function_ **![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438155478425)** **![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438168763033)** * The end user logs-in to Marvelous Designer with License ID * Use ‘Sign in with CLO-SET account’ or ‘Switch CLO-SET Account’ feature * CLO-SET accounts that are logged-in via software followed by above step, will be automatically added into Userpool ### **[Auto Add]** **:** What is Auto Add? * After the log-in to Marvelous Designer by License ID and signing in with a CLO-SET account inside of the Software (Sign in with CLO-SET, Switch CLO-SET Account), the CLO-SET Email is automatically added to the user pool of the corresponding License ID. _(Process)_ * Log in to Marvelous Designer with License ID ‘A’, and sign in with a CLO-SET account ‘B’ * This CLO-SET account ‘B’ will be added to user pool, underneath the License ID ‘A’ * If you switch the account to different CLO-SET account while using the software, then it will also be added to user pool, underneath the License ID ‘A’ * This option can be turned off at the License Account Admin - Userpool page. * ‘Auto Add’ option is only available for Onlineauth type of license. * ‘Auto Add’ will only work with License ID that has the email address attached. * If you try to assign members via ‘Auto Add’ option to the License ID that does not have an eligible email address attached, it will not function properly. ### **[Send Installer/ Delete]** ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438168906009) ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438156039705) * If you need to send out the installer for a certain version, or to make sure the end user received it well on their side, use the ‘Send Installer’ button. ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438203487001) * Also, the delete of member ID is available by clicking on the ‘Delete’ button * If a member is using more than one License ID, then you can choose License IDs you want to delete the member from. ### **[Name Edit]** **![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438219288217)** * You can assign nicknames to members for efficient management. This helps distinguish between members and take accurate actions. Use member names to simplify team management. ***ACCOUNT STATUS** * Not Integrated / Company blocked CLO-SET account Integration **![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438203817497)** * Not Integrated/ Company allowed CLO-SET account integration **![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438156861081)** * Integrated with CLO-SET **![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438204151961)** * Integrated (End User with Standalone License and have Sub Account(Member)) **![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438190725657)** ### **Offering by License Type:** * The Userpool feature allows you to manage access to your software license. Its functionality varies depending on your license type. ### [Network Online Licenses (Academic, Enterprise) and Linux License] * Adding Members: With these licenses, you can add an unlimited number of members to your Userpool using the "Add Member" feature. * Concurrent Users: While you can add as many members as you need, the number of users who can log in and use the software at the same time is limited by the number of licenses you own. ***Note:** If the number of concurrent users exceeds your license limit, users will not be able to log in. * Platform Restriction for Linux License: A member added for a Linux license can only use the software on the Linux OS. They will be unable to log in on Mac or Windows operating systems. *Note: If a Linux license member attempts to log in on an incompatible OS, an error will occur. ### [Enterprise Standalone, Personal, and Student Licenses] * Adding a Member: These licenses are limited to a single concurrent user, so you can only add one additional member using the "Add Member" feature. *Important: If you add a new Member, it will automatically replace and delete the previous one. * Concurrent Users: The concurrent user count for these licenses is one. This means that only one user, either the main account or the added Member, can be logged in at a time. * Note: The Standalone License will be retired as of November 30, 2025. For more information on this change, please refer to the[ ](https://www.google.com/search?q=link)Marvelous Designer Standalone License Transition. * Userpool feature summary by license type **License Type** | **Number of Members** | **Concurrent User** | **Supported Operating System** ---|---|---|--- Network Online (Enterprise, Academic) | Unlimited | Equal to the number of the licenses that you own | Win, Mac Linux | Unlimited | Equal to the number of the licenses that you own | Linux only Enterprise Standalone | One | One | Win, Mac Personal | One | One | Win, Mac Student | One | One | Win, Mac
content_description: The purpose of this webpage is to provide detailed information on the Userpool feature in Marvelous Designer 2024.2, facilitating enhanced license management and security for users integrated with CLO-SET.

title: Marvelous Designer to MetaHuman: USD Garment Integration Workflow
content: This guide outlines the workflow for exporting garments from Marvelous Designer as USD and integrating them with Unreal Engine **MetaHuman**. Step 1. Import USD Asset Step 2. Prepare MetaHuman Step 3. Create Cloth Asset Step 4. Configure Dataflow for Cloth Asset Step 5. Organize Assets Step 6. Create Outfit Asset Step 7. Configure Outfit Asset Step 8. Apply Outfit to MetaHuman ChaosCloth Asset Compatibility * * * ## Step 1. Import USD Asset ## ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/52799018460697) 1. In the **Content Drawer** , import your Clothing USD Asset created in Marvelous Designer into the desired folder. 2. Verify that the static meshes are correctly imported. ## Step 2. Prepare MetaHuman ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/52799018466585) 1. Locate your MetaHuman in the **Content Browser**. * Or, run it through the right-click Context Menu → MetaHuman → MetaHuman Character to create a new MetaHuman 2. **Double-click** the MetaHuman to open the **MetaHuman Editor**. 3. Export the MetaHuman as a **Combined Skeletal Mesh** : * MetaHuman Editor Main Menu → MetaHuman Creator → Export Combined Skel Mesh * Save this mesh inside the **Skeletal Meshes** folder of your USD asset directory. ## Step 3. Create Cloth Asset ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/52799079787033) 1. In the **Static Meshes** folder: * **Right-click** → **Physics > Cloth Asset**. * Name it clearly (e.g., CA_name). 2. **Open Cloth Asset in Dataflow Editor** : * Right-click the Cloth Asset → **Open in Dataflow Editor (Experimental)**. 3. **Clean up nodes** : * Delete everything except: * USD Import * Transfer Skin Weights * Remesh * Remesh LOD2 (optional for extra LOD) * Cloth Asset Terminal. ## Step 4. Configure Dataflow for Cloth Asset ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/52799641793433) 1. **Add Static Mesh Import Node** : * Right-click background → **Create Node: Static Mesh Import**. * Assign your USD static mesh to this node. 2. **Connect Nodes** : * Static Mesh Import → Transfer Skin Weights. * Transfer Skin Weights → Cloth Asset Terminal. * Also connect: * Transfer Skin Weights → Remesh → Collection LOD0. * Transfer Skin Weights → Remesh LOD2 → Cloth Asset Terminal (optional). 3. **Configure Transfer Skin Weights Node** : * Target Meshes: **Render Mesh**. * Render Mesh Transfer: **Skeletal Mesh**. * Transform Method: **Closest Point on Surface**. * Assign the **Combined Skeletal Mesh** to the Skeletal Mesh property. 4. **Preview** : * Switch the left window view to **Render** for visualization. ## Step 5. Organize Assets ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/52799881262873) 1. Create a new folder inside the Basic**Mesh** folder. 2. Move: * Static Mesh * Cloth Asset * Cloth Asset Node into this folder. ## Step 6. Create Outfit Asset ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/52799881264409) 1. In **Static Mesh Folder** : * **Right-click** → **Physics > Outfit Asset**. * Name it clearly (e.g., OA_name). 2. Select **Resizable Outfit Template** when prompted. 3. Move the Outfit Asset node into the folder created earlier. ## Step 7. Configure Outfit Asset ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/52800581027609) 1. **Open Outfit Asset in Dataflow Editor** : * Double-click the Outfit Asset. 2. Change **Evaluate Dataflow Graph** from **Automatic** to **Manual**. 3. **Add Source Asset** : * Select **Sized Outfit Source** → Click **+**. * Drag the Cloth Asset into the Source Asset option. * Assign a size name. 4. Click **Evaluate Dataflow Graph** and wait for completion. 5. Open **Source Body Slider** : * Drag and drop the Combined Skeletal Mesh. 6. Enable **Sized Outfit** checkbox to make it resizable. 7. Click **Evaluate Dataflow Graph** again, then switch back to **Automatic**. ## Step 8. Apply Outfit to MetaHuman ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/52800581029657) 1. Open MetaHuman Editor. 2. Go to the **Hair and Clothing** tab. 3. Drag and drop the **Outfit Asset** from the Content Drawer into the Outfit Clothing section. 4. In the Body tab, change the model's size parameters to adjust MetaHuman proportions, and confirm that the outfit adapts dynamically. 5. **Verify** that the outfit adjusts automatically to match the Metahuman's new size. ## ChaosCloth Asset Compatibility The use of ChaosCloth assets from USD data exported from Marvelous Designer is subject to the following compatibility restrictions based on the Unreal Engine version: * **Marvelous Designer 2025.0:** Compatible only with **UE 5.4**. * **Marvelous Designer 2025.2:** Compatible with **UE 5.6** and later version. * **UE 5.5:** Not compatible due to technical issues regarding simulation data. ※ Note: This issue is specific to **ChaosCloth**. Regular meshes and materials are unaffected.
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for exporting garments from Marvelous Designer as USD files and integrating them seamlessly with Unreal Engine's MetaHuman for enhanced character customization.

title: OBJ Trim Properties
content: ### Objective When an OBJ is imported as a Garment, input weight and reflect it in the Simulation. ### Location Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Edit Pattern [ Z ] / Transform Pattern [ A ] 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Pattern / Transform Pattern ### Operation 1. Select the tool/ menu indicated. 2. Select the loaded OBJ trim. →The OBJ properties are displayed in Property Editor. 3. Modify the properties according to the following. Information | Name | Enter a name and an item number of the trim. ---|---|--- Specification | Scale | Scale trim with X, Y, and Z-axis. Weight | Set the weight of trim. title: USD file Compatibility (ver. 12.1)
content: ## Feature Overview With USD, a graphics standard file format, you can increase collaboration productivity with a variety of 3D software You can export clothing, avatars, and accessories with meshes and materials from Marvelous Designer as USD files. You can also import USD files created in other 3D software packages into Marvelous Designer. ## Import USD You can import an USD file as an avatar, a trim, or a scene/prop type. Cloth and avatar animations can also be exported/imported. (ver. 2024.1) ### Steps Follow the indicated guideline below. **Location** Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ USD Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import (Add)▶ USD USD Layer Window ▶ Import Drag & drop an USD file on to the software **Setting - Import USD Dialog** Load Type | Open | All existing objects will be removed, leaving the imported file only. ---|---|--- Add | Add an object, keeping the existing objects. Object Type | Avatar | Import an USD file as an Avatar type. \- Objects imported as an Avatar type can be muti-selected. Trim | Import an USD file as a Trim type. \- The object will pass through the clothing while Simulation is on, as the Trim type cannot collide with clothing. \- Set the collide option for a Trim type on the Property Editor by toggling on the Collision check-box. \- Select an trim object and toggle on the Glue icon on the gizmo to attach the object to clothing. \- Toggle on the Scale icon on the gizmo to scale the size of an object. Scenes & Props | When importing an object as Scenes & Props, the object will pass through the clothing while Simulation is on, as the Scenes & Props type do not have Collision. Auto Create Fitting Suit | A Fitting Suit is automatically created in the import process. Scale | Scale | Set the unit of scale. % | Adjust the scale in percentage. Axis Conversion (ver.2024.1) | X, Y(Up), Z | Using Axis Conversion, you can change the orientation of the imported mesh. Select the up-axis used in the application where the file was imported from. Marvelous Designer will compare the up-axis of the incoming file and apply conversion if necessary. ※ Note : In Marvelous Designer, the Y axis is the up-axis. Invert | Invert the selected axis. Translation | Align Bottom to Ground | When an object is placed below the ground, toggle on Align Bottom to Ground check-box to place the object imported above ground. ※ Note (ver. 2024.1): * It is recommended that the Animation Layer name not be changed. * When importing an Avatar that is a USD file format, [Motion files (.MTN)](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358363172249) cannot be applied to that avatar because it is not the default skeletal avatar type supported by Marvelous Designer. * If multiple skeletal animations (SkelAnimation) are loaded into the animation window, the upper most animation is played in the 3D Space. ### End Result The USD file is successfully imported into the software you set. A list of layers for the imported file can be found on the USD Layer window. \- If USD Layer window is not visible in the workspace, it will appear in a new window as a pop-up. ## Export USD You can export clothing, avatars or trims as an USD file. Cloth and avatar animations can also be exported. (ver. 2024.1) ### Steps Follow the indicated guideline below: **Location** Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Export ▶ USD **Setting - Export USD Dialog** Prim | Mesh | Prim Path | Either select or deselect Mesh \- You can name the Prim Path for the Mesh when exporting. ---|---|---|--- Material | Prim Path | Either select or deselect Material \- You can name the Prim Path for the Material. \- When exporting the Material, a Texture folder is created within the folder where the USD is saved. All related textures will be saved in that Texture folder. Object | Select All Patterns | Either select or deselect all patterns. -Each pattern can be individually selected from the drop-down menu. Select All Avatars | Either select or deselect all avatars/objects \- Each avatar/object can be individually selected from the drop-down menu. Select All Graphics and Trims | Either select or deselect all graphics and trims \- Each graphic and trim can be individually selected from the drop-down menu. Single Object (ver. MD2024.0) | Exports selected object as a single object. Multiple Objects (ver. MD2024.0) | Exports selected object as multiple objects. Thin | Export USD without the rendering thickness. Thick | Export USD with the rendering thickness as Geometry. Unified UV Coordinates | Exports the texture data for all patterns to fit within UV coordinates Image Size | Set the size of the image in pixels Fill Texture Seams | Extend the scope of texture based on the texture's borders. Include Garment Simulation Data | USD export for garments, including the necessary data for simulation setup. Option (Ver. 2024.1) | Garment Animation (Ver. 2024.1) | Saves pattern cache animation. ※ Note : Since Pattern Cache Animation is exported as a mesh itself, there is no separate Animation Type prim. Avatar Animation (Ver. 2024.1) | Joint | Saves the animation data for Avatar animation as skeletal animation. ※ Note : Avatar Animation is exported to the USD Layer Window as a SkelAnimation type below SkelRoot. Cache (ver. 2024.2) | Saves Avatar cache animation. Basic | Scale | Set the unit of scale. % | Adjust the scale in percentage. Axis Conversion (ver. 2024.2) | Up Axis | Select the up-axis used in the application where the file was imported from. Marvelous Designer will compare the up-axis of the incoming file and apply conversion if necessary. ※ Note : In Marvelous Designer, the Y axis is the up-axis. ### ※ Note (Ver. 2024.1): * It is recommended that the Animation Layer name not be changed. * To export a pattern and an avatar at the same time, select the avatar first and then select the patterns. ### End Result The USD file is successfully exported as you set. \- When exporting the Material, a Texture folder is created within the directory where the USD is saved. All related textures will be saved in that Texture folder. ## USD Layer Window A list of layers for the imported file can be found in the USD Layer window. ### Steps Follow the indicated guideline below: **Location** The drop-down list at the top center of all windows. ▶ USD Layer ![usd_layer_window.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438538423577) **1\. Buttons** Create | Create an USD file \- An USD file is created with the specified path and name, appearing in the USD Layer window. This file will be set as the Authoring Layer. \- When exporting the Material, a Texture folder is created within the directory where the USD is saved. ---|--- Import | Import an USD file Clear | Delete all the layers listed in the USD Layer. **2\. List of Layers** Authoring Layer | The default layer which is being used at the moment. \- When running Export to USD Layer for clothing, trims, scenes/props, they will be exported to the Authoring Layer. ---|--- Material | The default path where the Materials appear. \- Users can name this path while running Export to USD Layer. Mesh | The default path where the Mesh appears. \- Users can name this path while running Export to USD Layer. **3\. Right Mouse Button****Menus - Layers** Click the right mouse button on the list of the layers to access the menus below. ![usd_layer_window2.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438532533785) Set Authoring Layer | Set the selected layer as active. \- The same can be done by double clicking the left mouse button** **This menu won't appear in the following situations: \- Where the selected layer is already set as the Authoring Layer. \- Where the selected layer is an USDZ (read only) \- Where the selected layer is missing. ---|--- Delete | Deleted the selected layer. This menu won't appear in the following situations: \- Where the selected layer is the Authoring Layer. Export USDZ from Layer | Export the selected layer as USDZ (read only) \- Once an USDZ is imported, it cannot be exported again. **4\. Export the Selected Object through Right Mouse Button Menus** To export your cloth and/or trim assets from Marvelous Designer as a USD file; select the assets from either 3D or 2D window, and click "Export to USD Layer" to export them to the Authoring Layer. This will update the USD file corresponding to the Authoring Layer. **Setting - Export to USD Layer** Prim | Mesh | Prim Path | Either select or deselect Mesh. \- You can name the Prim Path for the Mesh when exporting. ---|---|---|--- Material | Prim Path | Either select or deselect Material. \- You can name the Prim Path for the Material. \- When exporting the Material, a Texture folder is created within the folder where the USD is saved. All related textures will be saved in that Texture folder. Object | Single Object (ver. 2024.0) | Exports selected object as a single object. Multiple Objects (ver. 2024.0) | Exports selected object as multiple objects. Thin (ver. 2024.2) | Export USD without the rendering thickness. Thick (ver. 2024.2) | Export USD with the rendering thickness as Geometry. Unified UV Coordinates | Exports the texture data for all patterns to fit within UV coordinates Image Size | Set the size of the image in pixels Fill Texture Seams | Extend the scope of texture based on the texture's borders. Include Garment Simulation Data (ver. 2024.2) | USD export for garments, including the necessary data for simulation setup. Option (Ver. 2024.1) | Cache Animation (ver. 2024.1) | Saves pattern cache animation. ※ Note : Since Pattern Cache Animation is exported as a mesh itself, there is no separate Animation Type prim. Avatar Animation (ver. 2024.1) | Joint | Saves the animation data for Avatar animation as skeletal animation. ※ Note : Avatar Animation is exported to the USD Layer Window as a SkelAnimation type below SkelRoot. Cache (ver. 2024.2) | Saves avatar cache animation. Basic | Scale | Set the unit of scale. % | Adjust the scale in percentage. Axis Conversion (ver. 2024.2) | Up Axis | Select the up-axis used in the application where the file was imported from. Marvelous Designer will compare the up-axis of the incoming file and apply conversion if necessary. ※ Note : In Marvelous Designer, the Y axis is the up-axis. * When exporting garment using Export to USD Layer, the exported output will differ depending on the 3D Garment Rendering Style state. If the 3D garment appears in Thick Textured Surface, it will be exported with thickness. ### End Result The USD file is successfully exported as you set it. * When saving the project file (*.zprj), the imported USD Layer and file information will be saved altogether. \- When opening this file, if the USD file path is missing, you can either create new or ignore it. Create new USD file path in replace of the missing one, using the right mouse button menus. * Please try out this **[USD sample file](https://s3.marvelousdesigner.com/newmdweb/helpcenter/manual/KoiFish_USD.zip) **we created with Marvelous Designer and see how the new USD support can benefit your workflow. Step by step tutorial for how to export this USD file from Marvelous Designer coming soon.
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on importing and exporting USD files in Marvelous Designer, enhancing collaboration and productivity in 3D design workflows.

title: Modular Library (Ver. 2025.0)
content: **Table of Contents** Modular Library (2025.0) Structure of The Modular Library Group and Category Line Style Block Auto Modular Labeling Modular Configurator Save Style Save Block Modular Library Options ### ### ## Modular Library ### Objective Quickly and easily create different variations using previously saved garment blocks within Marvelous Designer. This section contains all of your blocks for mixing and matching different styles. Here you can also create and save: Groups, Categories, Styles, and Blocks. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Window ▶ Modular Library Side Panel Title Bar ▶ Right-click Dropdown Menu ▶ Modular Library ※Note: The buttons on the top right are: * **Add** (to add in a new Group or Category) * **List** (To switch between a list and icons) * **Refresh** (update to view any changes) #### ![a6e62ca1-0e8a-4a11-811f-2edb3f31548a](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438036249881) #### Structure of the Libraries By default, the Modular Library is organized by**Group, Category** and**Style.** This is where all of your blocks will be to mix and match different styles and blocks, here you can also create and save groups, categories, styles and blocks. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47358143614745)** **Group and Category** Both of these sections are Folder based; meaning you can bring in folders from anywhere you have access and also create folders anywhere you have access too. **![Modular Library.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47358143616409)** Both of these sections are Folder based; meaning you can bring in folders from anywhere you have access and also create folders anywhere you have access too. 1. Click ![add.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47358157785753) **Add** button to add your folder to a Group. 2. Doble-click the Group folder to navigate into the Category. 3. in Category stage, click ![add.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47358157785753) **Add** button and enter the name to add a new category. _**✨Tip:**_ You can copy the path or delete by right-clicking on a Group or Category folder. ### **![a6e62ca1-0e8a-4a11-811f-2edb3f31548a](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438036249881)** ## Group and Category ### Objective Both of these sections are Folder based; meaning you can bring in folders from anywhere you have access and also create folders anywhere you have access too. ### Operation ### Adding a New Group or Category 1. Click the Add (plus) button on the top Right, and click Add Group. Select the folder you want to add. → The selected folder will be added as a group. 2. Double-click the added group folder, and click the Add (plus) button on the top of the category tab and click Add Category. → The Add Category window appears. 3. Enter the category name and click the OK button. → The category is added to the selected group. ### Editing Group or Category 1. Select the folder you want to edit and Right click to see your options 1. Copy the Path → Path to the explorer folder is copied. 2. Delete → The folder is deleted. ### ## Line _This is an optional sub-category or "stage" between Category and Style._ Add a Line tier between Category and Style to create a more precise and detailed library structure. 1. Click ![add.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47358157785753) **Add** button in the Style stage and click **Group Style by Line** option. 2. In Add Line window, set the name and thumbnail and click **OK** button. → It becomes the upper level above Style in the hierarchy. This allows multiple styles to be grouped under a Line. 3. Click ![add.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47358157785753) **Add** button on the right side of the Line to add another Line. _**✨Tip:**_ When clicking **Add Line with Same Style** option, all Styles and Blocks within the selected Line are duplicated and added as a new Line. This can be useful when you want to reuse the same structure but make slight changes to some Styles or Blocks. 4. Right-click on the Line thumbnail to delete the selected Line or, change its thumbnail and name. #### ## ** **Style The style is the what all your blocks will be linked to. It is best to think of the different styles as a type of fit so that all your blocks can easily fit together when mixing and matching different blocks. #### ※ Note: The name of the group and category that this style is saved in, is at the top left. ![Modular Library1.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438081751833) ### Adding Style 1. After making Category, you can create Style. Double-click the category folder in which you want to add a style, and click the Add button on the top of the style tab. → Style Section window appears. → If there is a garment in the 3D window, the thumbnail for that garment is automatically registered. 2. If you want to register thumbnail manually, click the camera icon and open the image file. 3. Enter the name of the style and press OK button. → Style will be added with the thumbnail and the name. ### Editing Style 1. 1. Select the Style you want to edit and Right Click → The Style Selection pop up will come up again and allow you to change the Thumbnail, and Style Name. 2. Delete → If there are blocks within this style a Warning will pop up that the blocks included will be erased and to ask if you would still like to proceed. ![a6e62ca1-0e8a-4a11-811f-2edb3f31548a](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438036249881) ## Block These are the different pattern pieces that make up one full style. You can add in multiple patterns for one block, they will be what you will use to mix and create different variations of a style. ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438050383641) #### Adding a Block Section ※Note: For automatic block creation, please refer to the "Auto Block Creation" section below. 1. Click the thumbnail of the style that you want to add block, then click the Add (plus) icon and click Add Block Type on the top right. → Create Add Block Type window appears. ※ Note: Style needs to be added in order to add Block. 2. After setting the information below, click the OK button. Type | Set the block type ---|--- Tag | Enter the block tag. If you need to add 2 or more of the same type, categorize them through tags. When the types and tags are added in the same status, the existing block type will be overwritten. → the block type is added to the selected style. ### Adding a Pattern to a Block Section 1. 1. Within the added Block Section select the Add (plus) icon. → A Modular Creator pop up window will appear. 2. The Patterns for that block will then be selectable within the 2D window. → To select multiple pattern hold down the shift key → Once all the pattern are selected hit Enter on your key board 3. The Block Section window will pop up → The Block thumbnail will automatically be added based on 3D window → If you want to register a thumbnail manually you can select the camera icon to create New Thumbnail 4. The Thumbnail and name will automatically be added to the Block Section in the Modular Library ### Additional Options 1. Right-Click the block thumbnail you want to edit 2. Select the appropriate menu options as needed. Delete Selected Block | Deletes the selected Block. ---|--- Share Selected Block | Share the selected block with other styles. Any changes made to the block will apply to all shared instances. Change Thumbnail | Change the thumbnail. Replace with New Block | Replace the existing block with a new one. ### Auto Modular Labeling Auto Modular Labeling is based on the results learned from numerous pattern data and analyzes which part of the pattern it is based on only the shape of the pattern. 1. Click ![AI Active.svg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438036889369) **Auto Modular Labeling** button at the top right of the Style stage. → The automatically recognized blocks will be highlighted in colors corresponding to each block type. ![Modular Library3.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47358143655449) 2. Check all that all patterns in the 2D window are properly assigned to the correct block types using the Modular Creator. 2-1. If any patterns are not recognized correctly, you can manually adjust or relabel them by clicking **![edit.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47358157792665)Edit Block** button in the Modular Creator. 2-2. In the 2D window, select the patterns that match the block type you chose and then press the Enter key. _* You can select multiple patterns by holding the Shift key. _ 2-3. In Add Block File window, set the name and thumbnail and click**OK** button. _* The Block thumbnail will automatically be added based on 3D window._ 3. Click ![Button-1.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47358157793945) **Save Block** button to set thumbnail image and file name, then click **OK** button. → The Check mark will then be activated to signal that this block is ready. 4. Click**Add** button. 5. After checking whether the block pattern is sewn well with other block patterns, click **OK** button. _* If you need to reset the sewing line, click the Cancel button to correct the sewing line and try again._ ※Note: If you are adding a new block based on an existing block file, you can add it directly without going through the Modular Creator by clicking ![add.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47358157785753) Add button within each Block section, such as Front Body or Sleeves. ### ### ## Modular Configurator This is specifically for saving out style or blocks. This method brings you directly to the Modular Creator which makes saving out styles or blocks a little quicker. #### ### Save Style: 1. Select the Group & Category to save this style under → Can also create a new Group or Category using the add button at the top 2. Select the Add button to add a new Style 3. The Style Section Window will appear → If there is a garment in the 3D window, the thumbnail for that garment is automatically registered. 4. If you want to register thumbnail manually, select Create New Thumbnail and open the image file. 5. Enter the name of the style and press OK button. → Style will be added with the thumbnail and the name. #### ### Save Block: 1. Select the Group & Category to save this style under → Can also create a new Group or Category using the add button at the top 2. Select the Style to save the blocks under → Can also create a new style using the add button at the top 3. Add in the Block Type using the Add button at the top ※Note: Can also use the Auto Block Creation tool this will automatically add in all the blocks and assign all patterns to the coinciding blocks 4. Create New Block Type window appears. → After setting the information below, click the OK button. **Type** | Set the block type ※Note:→ the block type is added to the selected style. ---|--- **Tag** | Enter the block tag. If you need to add 2 or more of the same type, categorize them through tags. When the types and tags are added in the same status, the existing block type will be overwritten 5. The Patterns for that block will then be selectable within the 2D window. → To select multiple pattern hold down the shift key → Once all the pattern are selected hit Enter on your key board 6. The Block Section window will pop up. → The Block thumbnail will automatically be added based on 3D window → If you want to register a thumbnail manually you can select create New Thumbnail. 7. The Thumbnail and name will automatically be added to the Block Section in the Modular Library. ## ## Modular Library Options Here is where you can configure Modular setting / options. 1. Click Main Menu ▶ Settings ▶ Preferences ▶ Other in the top menu. Configure Modular Options as needed. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Default Folder** | Set the default location that the Modular Library saves the Style presets to. **Modular Access** | **Protect Modular Library to Restrict Editing** | Restrict all editing in the Modular Library to protect its original configuration. **Prevent Blocks Mix and Match across Different Styles** | To protect the users from apply different block fits together, turn on the option Prevent Mix and Match. When Prevent Mix and Match is active a Warning pop up will appear when a block from one style is being applied to a separate style. **Notch Sewing** | To save out a specific sewing relationship activate the Notching Sewing option. The Modular Sewing tags will then follow the notch placements for sewing relationships.
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to provide a comprehensive guide for efficiently utilizing the Modular Library in Marvelous Designer, enabling users to create, save, and manage various garment styles and blocks with ease.

content: ## Overview Marvelous Designer provides AI features as plug-in to support creators’ work. The default state is disabled, and the activation process may very depending on the license type. Follow the guide below to enable AI features and unlock new possibilities for creativity! ## License Type: Personal Individual users can control whether to enable or disable AI features in your account management page. 1. Log in to the [**Marvelous Designer Website**](https://www.marvelousdesigner.com/) with your account. 2. Go to **My Account → Account.** 3. Change the activation status of the **AI Studio Plug-In**. 4. The activation state will be applied after restarting the Marvelous Designer software. ## License: Enterprise For Enterprise License users, the availability of AI features for end users is managed by the account’s overall Administrator, in accordance with the company’s AI usage policy. Therefore, if you wish to activate AI features, please contact your company’s account administrator to request activation. Administrators can enable Marvelous Designer's AI features for their team according to their needs by following the guide below. 1. Log in to the [**Marvelous Designer Website**](https://www.marvelousdesigner.com/) with your Admin account. 2. Access the **License Account Admin > AI Studio Plug-In**. 3. Control **AI Feature Access** for each End-User with a License ID using the toggle. ## Available AI Feature #### AI Texture Generator (ver 2024.1) When you enter a keyword that symbolizes your envisioned design, the system will automatically generate a variety of fabric texture images related to that keyword. You can experiment with different ideas to produce multiple images, and then compare them to select the texture that best matches your desired style and mood. 📒[**Manual**](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358351055897--Beta-AI-Texture-Generator-Ver-2024-1) #### AI Graphic Generator (ver 2024.1) Simply type in a keyword, and a variety of graphic images related to that keyword will be automatically generated. You can then compare and select from the different versions to create a new graphic that matches your desired style and concept. 📒[**Manual**](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358161486361--Beta-AI-Graphic-Generator-Ver-2024-1) #### AI Pose Generator (ver 2025.1) You can easily create avatar poses using keywords or images. This feature allows you to intuitively bring your desired mood and movement to life without going through the complex process of 3D pose creation. 📒[**Manual**](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/en-us/articles/48920289920537-AI-Pose-Generator-Beta) #### AI Pattern Drafter (ver 2025.1) Enter keywords or upload an image to automatically generate measurements and create a drafted pattern for you. This allows you to produce a basic garment pattern without requiring detailed pattern-making knowledge or experience, enabling you to quickly begin creating a wide range of creative designs. 📒[**Manual**](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/en-us/articles/48920347302297-Pattern-Drafter-Beta) ## ##

title: Pleats
content: ## **Objective** Create the desired shape of pleats to Patterns. ## **Location** Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Pleats ▶ **Pleats** 2D Toolbar ▶ **![Pleats.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/51784511607961)Pleats** ## **Operation** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. 2. Click to create a start point and an endpoint of a reference line of the pleats along Pattern Outlines. → A Pattern is divided into two. 3. Click on the side where the pleats will be added. → The Pleats window appears. 4. Configure the options and select OK. **Pleats Type** | Select the type of the pleats (Knife, Box, or Accordion). ---|--- **Specification** | Number of Pleats | Decide the number of pleats. Depth | Assign the depth of the pleats (the depth of folded pleats). Interval | Set the interval between pleats when there are two or more pleats. Reverse Direction | Reverse the direction where the pleats will be added. **Option** | Assign fold angles to the fold lines. Greater the difference between the angle of Outside Fold and Inside Fold, sharper the folds are. → The pleats are created on the Pattern. → If there is an Internal Line in the Pattern, it is also moved and rotated along with the Pattern. **※ Note:** * If the segment where pleats are to be created is sewn to another Pattern, the pleats will be automatically sewn in place based on the pleat type selected. If the segment is not sewn, use the **Pleats Sewing** tool to sew the pleats to the other Pattern. * Pleats are dependent on segment point locations. When a pleat is started between two segment points, it will not go further than the next segment point and will result in an error/ red color to indicate this.
